terra.problem: Saying Moses would be the first to reject the answer invents his reaction without marking it as a guess.
The passage does not say Pharaoh had plenty of wealth.
The bank-statement joke makes light of the LORD displaying His power through thunder.
The claim that Israel receives laws later is a Bible fact outside this passage and needs a reference.
Calling the hail and lightning a show for the staff makes light of a destructive act of the LORD.
The reference to other plagues brings in Bible facts outside this passage without a reference.
The statement about the Israelites not yet living in Canaan brings in a Bible fact outside this passage without a reference.
The reference to Moses’s earlier years in Midian brings in a Bible fact outside this passage without a reference.
The text does not say Pharaoh is standing in the middle of the thunder and hail.
Saying Moses is not fooled implies Pharaoh is deceiving him. Moses says Pharaoh and his officials still do not fear the LORD, but the text does not say Pharaoh is trying to fool him.
The text says wheat and spelt were late crops, not that they had not come up yet.
